name: Thúy Vi Tông
stages: A new hall of pill furnaces rises on the eastern summit and the herb terraces climb another band of the slope.
A tall many-roofed pagoda crowns the lower summit facing the spiral path, and covered stairs link the herb terraces of both peaks.

name: Tùng Đào Cung
stages: A second terrace of halls climbs the far end of the ridge and the gallery gains a bell pavilion at its midpoint.
A tall many-roofed pagoda rises at the gallery's far end, and a broad stone stair road is cut down through the pines toward the city below.

name: Băng Tâm Các
stages: A second ice hall carved into the badland ridge behind the pavilion, and terraces of sword-practice grounds below it.
Twin frost-rimmed side towers flanking the main pavilion, joined by covered bridges, and a ring of cold wells mist-veiling the lower terraces.

name: Lạc Hà Tông
stages: More terraces climb the rise, a second ring of rose-tiled halls stands around the Sunset Ring, and a covered stair runs down toward the river market.
The terraces crown the whole swell; a tall many-roofed pagoda rises behind the Sunset Ring, and banners of rose silk hang along every terrace wall.

name: Thiên Xu Tông
stages: Covered stairs join the seven terraces, and a walled formation yard with stone array discs opens below the lowest hall.
Each terrace gains a tall pagoda so the Dipper line reads from far off, and a ring of warding pillars stands around the whole ridge.

name: Phượng Minh Cung
stages: A second ring of red halls and a covered music terrace climb the ridge around the great wutong, and a stair of red gates runs down toward Thiều Âm Thị.
A nine-roof pagoda rises beside the tree, nearly as tall as its crown, and the terraces spread along the whole ridge with a wutong planted on every step.

name: Thính Vũ Lâu
stages: New halls stack up the cone's flank on black stone terraces, each roof hung with its own rain-chains, and a covered stair climbs from the lake.
A second, lower tower rises on a shoulder of the cone, joined to the first by a roofed bridge; the whole slope is walled in dark stone, and still no window shows a light.

name: Hàm Nguyệt Trang
stages: Pearl sheds spread along the shore on both sides of the piers and the moon-viewing tower gains a fourth roof.
The manor walls take in the birch grove, a stone pearl hall rises behind the tower, and a second, smaller ring of white stones is laid in the shallows for the disciples.

name: Hồng Lô Cốc
stages: A second, taller furnace stack rises beside the first and the snow-free ring widens over a new terrace of drying sheds.
A stacked pagoda hall of red tile crowns the valley head above the furnaces, and a curved stone breakwater shelters the ash boats.

name: Vân Khởi Quán
stages: A row of hermit cells is cut into the cliff beside the platform and a stone path climbs to a second, higher terrace.
A stacked three-roofed sutra tower rises above the halls, and a covered walk follows the stream from the gate to the platform.

name: Vạn Hác Viện
stages: A second hall of practice rooms lines the far rim and a narrow stair is cut down the side of the pillar.
A tall three-roofed hall of the zither rises on the highest point of the rim, facing the pillar pavilion across the ravine.

name: Thải Chi Cốc
stages: More drying sheds and a stone furnace house with a tall chimney; the herb terraces climb further up both valley walls.
A second pagoda hall joined to the first by a covered stair, an upper grove of shaded lingzhi logs, and long orphan dormitories along the lower fields.

name: Lãng Đào Môn
stages: A covered slipway and a second hall for rope-makers; the watch pagoda gains a lantern storey to signal ferries at night.
A stone dock of its own on the river bend with rows of rebuilt ferries drawn up, and a four-roof pagoda rising behind the gate of hulls.

name: Cửu Cao Phái
stages: More roost towers out across the marsh and a long crane stable hall on the lower terrace.
A tall roost tower for the crane king beside a five-roof pagoda, and a stone landing terrace where riders come down from the sky.

name: Lê Hoa Am
stages: A meditation hall cut into the ice field edge and a wider ring of rimed pear trees.
A second bell pagoda higher on the slope, a covered stair between the two, and a walled guest court below for pilgrims.

name: Dạ Quang Môn
stages: A second ring of earth walls with stables, and a feasting hall with a dark tiled roof.
A tall watch pagoda over the caravan road and a row of glowing stone cups on the outer wall.

name: Trạc Anh Đài
stages: A second terrace is cut lower into the stream, a covered hall rises at the crest, and smokehouses for seal meat line the path up the rise.
The halls reach the crest under a tall watch pavilion, a stone stair joins every terrace, and the drying poles stretch in long bright rows down both banks.

name: Bình Thủy Môn
stages: A ferry hall rises by the quay, and a second tier of halls climbs the headland behind the main hall.
The headland is terraced to the point, a covered stair runs down to a stone pier, and the lantern mast is doubled with a second mast across the cove.

name: Mục Vân Trang
stages: A second stable hall and a long covered viewing gallery rise beside the track.
The manor climbs to a high riders' hall above the stable tower, and a second track loops out toward the coast with stone stands.

name: Thiên Bảo Trai
stages: An auction hall with a gilded double roof rises on a new terrace, and the furnace ring grows a second row.
The pagoda gains a higher tier with a gilt spire, and a walled treasury court with its own gate faces the market road.

name: Nam Phố Đường
stages: A second painted hall rises behind the first, joined by a covered gallery, and a walled yard of paper-drying lines spreads under the trees.
A three-roof scripture pavilion with cloud-painted beams rises above the forest canopy, ringed by scribes' cells and a small ink-grinding mill on a brook.

name: Củng Tinh Quán
stages: A second court with a star-map paved into its floor opens beside the armillary, and a covered walk leads down to the lakeshore.
A tall three-roof observation tower rises over the abbey, its open top deck facing the pole, and the walls take in the near shore of the lake.

name: Thối Tinh Môn
stages: A second cascade of troughs and a walled ore yard open beside the first, and the forge hall gains a third roof.
A tall smoke tower of black stone crowns the seat, and a covered stair runs from the forges down to the mine road.

name: Phất Y Cốc
stages: A walled practice yard of raked sand and a row of guest lodgings for hiring patrons stand below the gate.
A tall sword pavilion of three plain roofs rises at the valley head, with a stone stair to a meditation ledge above, and still no name carved anywhere.

name: Trúc Thực Viên
stages: A second terrace of seed bamboo and a woven-bamboo seed store join the garden, and a beast pen of woven bamboo stands at the edge.
A tall three-roof hall of bamboo and red timber rises over the beds, with stepped seed terraces spreading from it like a fan.

name: Lễ Tuyền Phái
stages: A second pagoda roof and a wine cellar dug into the rise; the spring basin gains a carved stone canopy and a covered walk runs down to the lake.
The whole rise is terraced with herb courts and a guest hall for the Pivot's envoys; a white balustrade rings the wutong and a long jar store lines the shore.

name: Hồng Đậu Trang
stages: A guest wing on stilts over the shore and a walled poison garden behind the halls; the moon gate gains a twin on the sea side.
Three walled courts climb the slope to a red pagoda where Phi Hồng is kept; the bean vines now cover the whole outer wall.

name: Xuyên Lâm Môn
stages: A second staff house at the foot of the stair, and a roofed rest hall halfway down for travellers.
A walled mountain gate with a training court cut into the ridge and a covered stair running the full way down into the forest.

name: Phần Vũ Đường
stages: A second tier of halls and a walled court around the sitting vents, with a stone bath for the burned.
A stepped red-stone hall rises high over the whole vent field, and the black mast stands on its top terrace.

name: Yên Ba Thành
stages: The walls extend up the river bank and a second quay with green-roofed warehouses lines the river mouth.
A great stone harbour gate spans the river behind the mole, and the upper town's green roofs climb a terraced hill clear of the mist.

name: Hàn Tân Thành
stages: The walls reach the far bank and a fortified bridge-gate rises at the middle of the ford.
A tall beacon tower stands over the harbour, and a second line of pillars marks a deep channel for larger ships.

name: Tùng Gian Thành
stages: The walls grow to take in a new pine grove, and a carved timber hall with a double roof rises behind the moon gate.
A second moon-viewing terrace tower stands above the harbour, and a stone mole extends the port into the sea.

name: Đào Thanh Thành
stages: A second row of wharf warehouses along the high quays and a pine-roofed listening terrace on the upper wall.
An outer wall reaching to the forest edge, a covered bridge over the river, and a five-roof bell pagoda that answers the pine waves.

name: Khai Dương Thành
stages: A stone sea mole with warehouses along it, and a second bronze disc on the river gate.
An outer harbour wall, a lighthouse tower on the mole, and a new walled quarter climbing the riverbank inland.

name: Trường Vân Thành
stages: A second caravan gallery branching to a new dock, and a stone caravanserai inside the land gate.
An outer wall around the docks, a lighthouse on the river mouth, and a taller ward formation pagoda at the city's centre.

name: Liên Giang Thành
stages: The roofed bridge is doubled with a second span, new ice-houses line the quays, and the walls take in the fishers' quarter on the far bank.
A tall grey drum tower rises over the harbour, the quays run out in stone piers to the sea, and both banks are walled to the forest edge.

name: Đàm Ảnh Thành
stages: A painters' hall with long open galleries rises on the pool's north side, and the river quay is rebuilt in stone.
A second walled ward takes in the river's far bank, and a tall pavilion over the water is built so its reflection completes it in the pool.

name: Nhạn Thanh Thành
stages: A great wool exchange with a long grey roof rises by the harbour, and the walls take in the dyers' quarter.
A second winged tower is raised over the river gate, and stone wool warehouses line both banks to the sea.

name: Tử Điện Thành
stages: A second armoury hall with violet tile rises inside a new inner wall, and the harbour gains a war-boat slip.
The walls are doubled on the landward side with gate towers, and the ward array's shimmer brightens into a clear violet dome over the bay front.

name: Tinh Hán Thành
stages: The wall runs the whole shore, a second stone quay reaches out from the bone reef, and a lighthouse tower rises at the reef's end.
A grand harbour hall with a three-roof pagoda faces the sea, the reef is armoured with dressed stone between every rib, and the formation's pillars glow faintly along the walls at dusk.

name: Lai Nghi Thành
stages: The nine-tier terrace gains a roofed musicians' gallery and the harbour a second mole lined with warehouses.
A second wall ring takes in the river quays; the terrace is faced in red-lacquered stone and a tall ceremonial gate opens on the sea.

name: Thu Trì Thành
stages: The pools climb higher up the hill as the upper town grows; a second harbour basin and a long covered hall for the Night Rain trade.
A walled upper city of dark halls looks down over the tiered pools; the market's awnings spread across three terraces and the harbour is walled in stone.

name: Không Mông Thành
stages: The arcades reach the harbour quays, and a drum tower rises at the main crossing.
A second wall ring up the valley sides; covered bridges link the arcades across the river, and the harbour gains a stone breakwater.

name: Ngũ Thải Thành
stages: A sixth ward of plain grey roofs for newcomers and a stone breakwater for the harbour.
A second wall ring up the river, and a five-roofed hall of the potters' guilds at the city's heart.

name: Lam Yên Thị
stages: A second side stair of stalls branches off halfway up, and an inn with a double grey roof stands at the foot.
A covered market hall straddles the stair's midpoint, and a stone gate arch marks the market's lower entrance.

name: Tùng Hạ Thị
stages: A second, outer ring of stall-houses is begun and a caravan yard is fenced beside the gate.
A round two-storey market hall rises in the centre of the ring, and a timber palisade with a roofed gate encloses both rings.

name: Đào Sa Thị
stages: A raised boardwalk links the stalls to a rebuilt landing, with a red-doored assay house at its head.
A market square on piles behind a timber palisade, a small customs pagoda flying Tùng Đào's colours, and washing cradles out to the far sandbars.

name: Tống Khách Thị
stages: A walled inn yard joins the market, and the stalls double along the road under longer eaves.
The market gains a gate and a covered street, and a second, larger pavilion rises beside the old one, which is kept exactly as it was.

name: Tương Phùng Thị
stages: A stone quay with warehouses anchors the raft, and the boats spread into two lashed arms.
A covered market hall stands on piles over the water, and the raft rings it in a wide floating crescent.

name: Vật Hoa Thị
stages: A covered arcade rings the square and a caravan yard is walled in beside the road.
A stone exchange hall with a high double roof faces the scale, and the market's walls take in a second square.

name: Hạc Đinh Thị
stages: More islets are joined; a timber market hall on piles stands at the centre of the causeways, and a ferry landing serves the sect road.
The causeways become a raised stone walk on low arches across the whole shoal, with a two-roof market tower at its heart; the cranes still stand below.

name: Thiên Quyền Thị
stages: A second gantry and a covered arcade of money-changers' stalls ring the square, and a stone weights hall with bronze doors stands on its north side.
The market is walled and gated in stone, with a drum tower over the gantries and a long caravan yard on the road toward Thạch Kiều Thành.

name: Thiều Âm Thị
stages: A covered market hall of bamboo and a second stage on the far bank join the lanes, with a footbridge between them.
The market is walled with a red gate tower, a drum tower and an instrument-makers' guild hall, and a stone landing takes the river boats.

name: Hạnh Hoa Thị
stages: A covered flower hall at the market gate and a stone quay on the river.
A second walled quarter of healers and herb sellers; the apricot grove is walled as a market garden.

name: Quy Điểu Trấn
stages: The wall runs further along the shore and the nest poles stand in double rows; a stone pearl market hall rises by the harbour.
A second harbour basin is cut, and a tall grey-roofed bird-watching tower stands over the shore where the winter ice market is held.

name: Mục Ca Thành
stages: A second ring of folds is built and a long covered wool hall rises inside the walls.
A tall drum-and-song tower stands at the city's centre, and the harbour gains a stone mole for the wool ships.

name: Bạch Sa Trấn
stages: A merchants' quarter of two-storey warehouses grows inside an extended wall and the pier is rebuilt in stone.
A tall double-roofed clan hall of the Thẩm stands at the town's heart, and a small harbour wall curves around the rows of net frames.

name: Bách Diệp Trấn
stages: The grid is extended along the river and an incense workshop quarter is added inside a longer wall.
A tall cypress-wood hall of the incense guild rises at the town's heart, and a stone quay lines the river mouth.

name: Tiều Ca Trấn
stages: A second flume comes down a neighbouring ridge and a sawmill house stands over the log pond.
A stone harbour wall shelters the timber ships, and a tall woodcutters' guild hall rises inside the walls.

name: Lộc Minh Trấn
stages: A carvers' quarter of open workshops spreads along the river bank and the ferry pier is doubled.
A tall carved timber hall of the Lâm clan rises over the town, and a stone ferry landing replaces the old pier with the stag moved to its end.

name: Cổ Độ Thành
stages: A smiths' quarter with tall chimneys grows outside the river gate, and a second ferry stair is built downstream.
A tall drum tower of the ferrymen rises over the stair, and the walls take in the smiths' quarter and a stone river quay.

name: Hà Bạn Trấn
stages: A second waterwheel and a stone mill house, with a covered herb wharf along the bank.
The wall runs along the river with a water gate, and a row of mills turns in a cut channel beside the town.

name: Lâm Hạ Trấn
stages: More round granaries on staddle stones and a timber fence around the storehouse quarter.
A stone granary hall with a tall vented roof under the oldest beeches, and a full town wall with a grain gate on the river.

name: Bích Khê Trấn
stages: A carvers' street with a covered market, and a stone footbridge across the green brook.
A larger wall, a jade hall with a green-glazed roof, and weirs stepping the brook far upstream.

name: Thanh Bách Thành
stages: A second market quarter inside the walls and a shrine pavilion on the crater pond's rim.
An outer wall enclosing the crater pond, and a tall tax hall with stacked roofs among the oldest cypresses.

name: Hòe Âm Trấn
stages: A stone quay with a hunters' market, and the locust avenue extended further up the mountain road.
A larger wall with a harbour gate, a Tiêu family hall with a two-tier roof, and a waystation for Lê Hoa Am's pilgrims at the avenue's end.

name: Hồi Lan Thành
stages: A rice market quarter and warehouses along the inner breakwater.
A second hooked breakwater forming a full harbour ring, with a watch pagoda at its tip and a walled merchant quarter outside the old wall.

name: Mộc Lan Thành
stages: A fur market hall with a high grey roof rises behind the quay, and the magnolia rows run on along a new sea wall.
The walls take in the beach quarter, a stone breakwater shelters the harbour, and a three-roofed gate tower faces the volcano inland.

name: Kê Minh Trấn
stages: The harbour wall is lengthened into a stone pier and a fish market roof rises by the gate.
A second ring of wall takes in the poultry yards and net sheds, and a covered gatehouse lifts the rooster pole higher still.

name: Xích Ngạn Trấn
stages: A pigment mill and drying yard sit inside the walls, and a second stair is cut to a new landing.
The town fills the clifftop, a stone pier runs out from the cove, and a tall grey-tile hall overlooks the sea from the cliff edge.

name: Hải Yến Trấn
stages: Tall nest houses with many tiers of eaves rise inside the walls, and the harbour gains a stone quay.
A ring of nest towers stands along the walls, and a nest market hall with a high grey roof faces the harbour.

name: Triều Âm Thành
stages: The breakwater is lengthened along the river mouth and a customs hall rises at the harbour gate.
A second harbour basin is walled in, and a tall bell-less listening tower stands on the breakwater's end, open to the sea wind.

name: Thanh Điền Trấn
stages: A walled horse yard joins the town and the hitching rails double along the road.
A granary row and a fair ground with a viewing stand rise beside the walls.

name: Thảo Đường Thành
stages: A new granary ward is walled in and more ponds are dug in rows along the road.
A tall grain hall with a double roof rises at the city's heart, and canals link the pond grid to the sea.

name: Ngư Lương Trấn
stages: A fish market roof and smoking sheds rise on the bank by the weir.
A second weir is built upstream and the walls take in both banks, joined by a footbridge along the old weir.

name: Liễu Ngạn Trấn
stages: The levee is faced with stone and a drum house is built beside the flood-pillar.
A stone river gate and a sluice tower guard the town, and the levee runs on past the walls on both sides.

name: Hòa Phong Trấn
stages: A house of healing with a long open veranda rises facing the sea.
The town grows a seaside terrace of guesthouses for the sick, each with its own tall wind-scoop, and a stone quay for the boats that bring them.

name: Ngũ Cốc Thành
stages: A guild hall for the grain towers rises behind the quay, and a breakwater shelters the ships.
A second row of grain towers is built on a new pier, and the walls take in the barge canal from the plain.

name: Phong Lâm Trấn
stages: The wall reaches the waterline, a stone quay takes larger boats, and a second clan hall rises opposite the Tạ hall.
A curved harbour mole runs out under the maples, a two-storey gate tower stands on the sea wall, and the Tạ hall gains an upper storey whose new eaves the swallows fill within a spring.

name: Tang Ma Thành
stages: Weaving halls and silk-dyeing yards spill outside the wall, and a stone gatehouse rises over the main rope bridge.
A second wall rings the rope walks and dyeworks, a tall drum tower stands at the centre, and the lattice of rope bridges spreads over every channel, hung with silk pennants.

name: Thạch Kiều Thành
stages: A second wall takes in the caravan yards on both banks, and a tall drum tower rises at the bridge's north end.
The city spreads across both banks in a double grid, with a three-roof Hall of the Compact beside the bridge, bell towers on every gate, and stone embankments lined with river barges.

name: Song Kiều Trấn
stages: A second wall takes in an ore yard beside the bridges, and an Ôn clan hall with a two-storey gate faces the toll pier.
The town spreads across both banks inside one wall, with a drum tower over the square and a stone assay hall raised over the open scales.

name: Mạch Điền Trấn
stages: A second granary on staddle stones and a stone harbour wall join the town, and the town wall is extended to the quay.
A row of great granaries stands along the harbour, with a granary-master's hall and a drum tower over the gate.

name: Thanh Khê Thành
stages: A second wall takes in shipyards along the brook, and a stone harbour arm doubles the anchorage under the lanterns.
A red gate tower stands at the harbour mouth, a three-roof harbour hall faces the gulf, and the lantern row runs round the whole enlarged harbour.

name: Hoàng Vân Thành
stages: A second ring of granaries rises outside the walls and a stone grain wharf runs along the river.
A walled granary district with a yellow-roofed counting hall at its heart; a canal basin is cut from the river for the barges.

name: Đạo Hương Trấn
stages: The Vương build an ancestral hall facing the row of stones, and the town walls are faced in brick.
A second walled quarter for rice merchants and a stone-paved field road; the row of generation stones now runs to the river.

name: Lục Dã Trấn
stages: A drying pavilion for herbs and a walled seed garden of Lễ Tuyền Phái beside the town.
A brick-walled town with a healers' hall at the gate, and the herb chequer spread far across the meadows.

name: Bình Dã Trấn
stages: A second drying yard outside the walls and roofed sheds to store the mats.
A brick-walled town with a raised drying terrace on every rooftop and a merchants' hall facing the great yard.

name: Xuân Thảo Thành
stages: A second turf-capped wall ring and a stone bridge over the river with a market at its foot.
A walled forest-trade city with a timber hall on a grassy mound at its heart, its own roof turfed like the walls.

name: Lãng Hoa Thành
stages: A second harbour mole with its own blowholes, and stone salt pans along the shore.
A walled upper town around the watch hall, and a long spray wall running the whole bay.

name: Vọng Hải Trấn
stages: A walled signal post joins the towers along the cliffs, and a fishing harbour is dug in the river mouth.
A brick-walled coastal town with a beacon hall and a covered stair from the harbour to the towers.

name: Phong Đăng Trấn
stages: A walled granary yard for the tax grain and a stone quay for the boats.
A brick-walled town with the Lục family's manor on a rise and a second steelyard over the harbour gate.

name: Thạch Cơ Thành
stages: A second jetty beside the first and a walled shipyard on the shore.
A fortified harbour city with a stone lighthouse at the red end of the jetty and a sea wall around the anchorage.

name: Tang Điền Trấn
stages: A reeling house by the shore and more silkworm sheds in the outer fields.
A brick-walled silk town with a dye works and a stone pier for the silk boats.

name: Thu Phần Các
stages: A walled grave court with a ward-stone at each corner, and a second tower for the soul arts.
Terraced halls climb the whole hill, and the slip strings reach down to its foot.

name: Tử Điện Thành
project: Great gathering array (Tụ Linh Đại Trận)
stages: survey stakes and nine foundation stones set in a ring around the place
stone pillars carved with array script standing in the ring
the pillars lit, faint golden qi lines joining them over the roofs
a second, outer ring of lit pillars, the qi lines now drawing one visible array figure over the whole place
the array figure glowing on the ground across the place, a soft pillar of light at its centre and the clouds above drawn into a slow spiral

name: Đào Khê Thôn
stages: a fresh trench cut toward the place from the nearest high ground
a stone-lined channel with sluice gates reaching the place
the channel glowing faintly, a soft mist where it meets the place

name: Lạc Hà Tông
stages: marked slopes and the first low terrace walls on the hill beside the place
terraced fields stepping up the hill
the terraces green with spirit herbs, a small gathering stone at the top

name: Đào Thanh Thành
stages: anchors and the first planks driven into the nearest cliff
a stair and plank road climbing the cliff face
a roofed sky bridge with lanterns spanning the gap
a second sky bridge and a lantern-lit waystation pavilion built halfway up the cliff

name: Đào Sa Thị
stages: a cleared square and timber frames at the edge of the place
covered halls and warehouses around the square
a walled trade quarter with a tall guild hall and plain coloured banners
the quarter grown past its old walls: a second guild hall, caravan yards and long rows of warehouses

name: Khai Dương Thành
stages: piles and a rubble mole reaching into the water
a stone breakwater and quays
a lighthouse pagoda at the breakwater's end
a second breakwater closing a full harbour basin, with dry docks and a customs hall on the quay

name: Thiên Xu Tông
stages: an earth rampart and stakes around the place
stone walls with gate towers around the place
the walls hung with ward talismans and a faint dome of ward light over the place
a second, outer wall with watchtowers, and the ward dome bright and banded with script

name: Nam Phố Đường
stages: a cleared stone terrace inside the place
a three-storey pavilion rising in bamboo scaffolding
a five-storey library pagoda with a brass roof finial

name: Thải Chi Cốc
stages: a stone platform and a flue at the edge of the place
a furnace hall with a tall chimney
the furnace hall with a glowing furnace mouth and a column of pale coloured smoke

name: Phụ Tinh Phong
stages: a cleared path and marker stones beside the natural feature
a small open pavilion with a ring of stone lanterns beside the feature, the feature itself untouched
